body:
I think I've got a fix for this!

From my investigation, the problem seemed to be that the parent expression of `KEY_0` was being recognized as an enum type, and as a result it was also assigning the enum type to `KEY_0` itself. As a result, when you typed `KEY_0.` it wanted to suggest possible enum values for the enum type that `KEY_0` belonged to.

My notes:

> C++ enum values and user-defined enum values have `r_type.kind = 0 (GDScriptParser::DataType::BUILTIN)` and `builtin_type = 2 (Variant::INT)`
> Example:
> ```gdscript
> enum { ONE, TWO }
> enum MyEnum { THREE, FOUR }
> ...
> var i = KEY_0. <-- int
> var j = Key.KEY_0. <-- int
> var k = ONE. <-- int
> var l = MyEnum.THREE. <-- int
> ```
> (Note that `Key` by itself is not considered a constant, apparently.)
> 
> User-defined named enums' names have `r_type.kind = 0 (GDScriptParser::DataType::BUILTIN)` and `builtin_type = 27 (Variant::DICTIONARY)`
> Example:
> ```gdscript
> enum MyEnum { ONE, TWO }
> ...
> var i = MyEnum. <--- 
> var j = MyEnum.ONE <-- (no period after name)
> ```

I am able to stop the bad behavior without (to my testing so far) introducing any new bad behavior and with minimal, self-contained changes to `gdscript_editor.cpp` - will open a PR for them soon.
